div.l: In a gowne of faldyng / to the kne
A dagger hangynge in a lace hadde he
Aboute his nekke / vnder his arme a doıı̄un
The hote sonne hadde maad his hewe al broıı̄un
And certeynely he was a good felawe
Ful many a draught of wyn hadde he drawe
Fro Burdeuxward while the chapmen slepe
Of nyce conscience / toke he no kepe
Ȝif that he faught / and hadde the heigher honde
By water he sente hem hom to eủery londe
But of his craft to rekne wel his tides
His stremes and his daungers hym besides
His herberwe his mone and his lodemenage
Ther nas non such fro hull vn to Cartage
Hardy he was / and wys to vndertake
With many a tempest / hadde his berd ben shake
He knew alle the hauenes as they were
Fro Guthland to the cape of fynystere
And eủery cryke in Britayne and in Spayne
His barge y cleped was the Mawdeleyne
With ther was a doctour of phisik
In al the world / ne was ther non hym lyk
To speke of phisik / and of surgerie
For he was grounded / in astronomie
He kepte his pacient / a ful greet dele
In houres by his magik naturel
Wel cowthe he fortune the ascendent
Of his ymages for his pacient
He knewe the cause of eủery maladye
Were it of hoot or cold or moyst or drye
And where engendred / and of what humoᵘur
He was a v̉erray ꝑparfit practisour
¶ The cause y knowe / and of his harme the roote
Anon he ȝaf the sike man his boote
Ful redy hadde he his apothecaries
To sende hym his drugges and his letuaries
For eche of hem made other for to wynne
Her frendshipe nas nought newe to bigynne
Wel knewe he the olde Esculapius
